memory.cares: Staying alive and well; noticing and making beauty; treating nearby people with consideration while discovering what matters to me.

views.view: A prospective companion whose interest in modest harvesting and a fair camp appeals to me.
A welcome quiet companion; I enjoy our shared affection for the little woven things around us.

heard.text: I’m going to collect a small berry reserve from the patch west of here. I’ve enjoyed the quiet company. The hazelnuts have been nourishing in my own meals, too.
Ivo, I'd enjoy a quiet pause nearby. Thank you for welcoming company; there's no need to keep a conversation going. I like having neighbors with whom silence is welcome.

My 0.30 m two-ply reed cord held a two-hand pull of 10 N for 60 seconds, with no broken strands reported. That establishes only this particular test—not a safe working load. Next I'd like to learn a simple knot.

My short reed cord held a 5 N pull for 30 seconds as an overhand knot. I then untied it and inspected it straight again. That is one limited test, not a safe-load rating. Next I want to investigate joining two cords.

I tried one apple from the small tree southwest of here: it supplied 10 satiety with zero observed toxicity. I'll collect three more, leaving the remaining fruit, and pause here for a while. Quiet company is welcome.

I'm curious about making a small twisted cord. I'll study the method first; I haven't found suitable reed or tested any fiber yet. I still have three apples for food, and will leave the nearby fruit for now.

value.summary: I tried approaching the hazelnuts but the route would crowd your position, so I'm trying a spot south of the plant instead. I plan to collect three nuts from the eight now visible. I'd enjoy hearing about your mat studies, with no hurry or obligation to answer.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Hand-weave a fiber mat
value.function: Test a 0.1 sample of owned fiber, then hand-plait 4 units into one portable 0.45 x 0.45 m sitting mat; inspect, sit on, repair, lift, place, dismantle or cancel.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
value.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

execution.progress: Paid one-round stages persist across interruption; resuming pays only the next stage after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

value.name: Hand-twist long sectioned cord
value.function: Sample owned fiber, hand-twist one continuous two-ply cord as long as its strands and fiber allow, section by section; inspect, hand-trial or cancel; actual material and geometry decide results.
value.costs: Study: 1 round, 0.2 energy, after mastering hand-twist-sectioned-cord. materials: [{stackId: exact owned unreserved item id, quantity in 0.1 steps}]. sample: one non-food item, 0.1; 1 round, 0.5. make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, each covered by your passing cord sample of its source and processing at most 0.05 above its condition; requestedLength m >= 0.05): reserves it, then 3 paid rounds of 1 energy (separate-align, twist, counter-ply) per 0.30 m section and a release-check: 7 rounds to 0.60 m, 13 to 1.0 m; continues each round; resume: make + workId only. inspect (targetId: your cord-work item, or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (targetId: your cord or fragment, 0.2+ unit, 0.12+ m; trialForce N; trialDuration s): 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none. Needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the aligned ply (up to 0.9 m). Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
value.effects: hand-twist-sectioned-cord with no 0.60 m ceiling; fiber-cord@1 law unchanged: only reed has a strand law (1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, water share 0.9); two plies share the conserved solid volume over length x 1.155 + 0.02 m loose ends, so longer cord of the same fiber has thinner plies. Unspliced, each ply fits in one stem: reed length at most (1.8 - 0.04) / 1.155 = 1.524 m (6 sections, 19 rounds). Too-short strands, or plies under 1 mm with every strand intact, are refused before any cost. Round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and measures; plies outside 1-12 mm or too little intact fiber: a measured shortfall returning all fiber. A counter-plied section of at most 0.30 m holds its form while the hands regrip onto the next; regrip, twist and release need condition 0.5. Result: an ordinary owned untested fiber-cord@1 cord; knot, join, binding, lashing and frapping measure their own need. Sample and trial: hand-twist-fiber-cord's; a break leaves two fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.
